name: Nuru Tamarind-Chili Spark
description: A sharp, tangy carbonated drink blending synth-tamarind with real chili extract and a whisper of smoked sea salt. The heat builds slow and lingers, making it a favorite for long shifts on the Tier 2 factory floors.
flavor_profile: Tart tamarind up front, warm chili bloom mid-palate, finishing with a briny, smoky edge and effervescent bite
cultural_context: Nuru Tamarind-Chili is the unofficial drink of the overnight shift — vending machines in Tier 1-2 manufacturing blocks are rarely without it. Workers call it 'the wake-up slap.' It has a loyal following among chrome-augmented laborers who say the chili interacts interestingly with certain neural dampeners.
story_hooks: A batch of Nuru Tamarind-Chili from a specific Shelf vending machine has been causing mild synesthetic episodes — someone spiked the syrup supply, and the trail leads back to a BCI-modification black market.
A Tier 2 labor organizer uses Nuru distribution routes as cover for passing encrypted messages between cells — the cans themselves are data carriers.

A Tier 4 food critic wrote a viral piece calling Nuru 'the most honest drink in Meridian 88,' causing a brief, uncomfortable class-tourism craze where Spire residents descend on Shelf vending machines.
